subject: Urban Planning
title: Day Zero: Cape Town's Water Crisis
description: A short lesson to help you apply Day Zero: Cape Town's Water Crisis.

hook.text: In 2018, Cape Town nearly became the first major city in the world to run out of water. They called it Day Zero.

buildup.text: Three years of drought emptied reservoirs to 13% capacity. The city prepared to shut off taps for 4 million people.

discovery.text: Residents were limited to 50 liters per person per day — about a 90-second shower and a few toilet flushes.

twist.text: Cape Town avoided Day Zero through dramatic conservation. Water use dropped 50% in months. Behavior changed overnight.

climax.text: São Paulo, Chennai, Mexico City, and Los Angeles all face similar water crises. Cape Town was a preview, not an anomaly.

punchline.text: The taps almost went dry for 4 million people. It can happen to any city.

quiz.question: How did Cape Town avoid running out of water?
options: Emergency desalination plants were built in three months
Residents cut water use by 50% through dramatic conservation
Neighboring countries donated water through emergency pipelines
